title: Italian Seasoning
description: Italian Seasoning is a classic herb blend that combines fragrant Mediterranean herbs into a versatile, restaurant-quality seasoning. Balanced, aromatic, and herb-forward, this blend enhances pasta sauces, pizzas, roasted vegetables, marinades, dressings, and grilled meats while delivering authentic Italian flavor without overpowering the dish.

ingredients.title: Ingredients (by weight—chef standard for accuracy)
items: 4 g dried rosemary, lightly crushed (about 1 tbsp)
2 g dried savory (about 2 tsp) — optional but adds depth
1 g crushed red pepper (about ½ tsp) — subtle restaurant heat
1 g garlic granules (about ½ tsp) — very light, so it enhances without dominating

instruction.title: Step 1 – Crush the Robust Herbs
steps: Place rosemary and sage in your hand and rub to break them slightly; this releases aroma and gives a more refined texture.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Mix All Herbs Evenly
steps: A small whisk or gloved hand works best.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Rest the Blend
steps: Seal in an airtight container and let it sit 12–24 hours before use.
This allows volatile aromas to marry—standard restaurant practice.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Store Properly
steps: Keep sealed, away from heat and light.
Best flavor: 3–4 months, though safe up to a year.

servingSuggestions.title: How Chefs Use This Blend (Pro Tips)
items: Bloom the herbs: Add the seasoning to warm olive oil for 20–30 seconds before adding anything else. This wakes up the dried herbs and produces a deeper, rounder flavor.
Use late in cooking for bright dishes: For tomato sauces and seafood, add the blend in the last 5 minutes to avoid bitterness.
Use early for roasted meats/veg: Dry herbs develop beautifully with heat.
Add fresh herbs at the end (restaurant secret): A pinch of fresh basil, parsley, or thyme at plating elevates the dried blend into fine dining territory.

chefTips: High-end kitchens avoid strong powdered garlic/onion. They use a touch only for balance.
Balanced, aromatic, herb-forward, not overly “Americanized,” with professional subtlety.
Works exceptionally well for pasta sauces, pizza, roasted vegetables, pasta salads, dressings & marinades.
Excellent as an Italian-style rub for chicken, pork, or fish.
